newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip decline.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip decline.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks were dragged down by a highly capitalised blue chip on Wednesday as investors searched for direction and waited for foreign activity to pick up after the Chinese Lunar New Year, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.01 points down at 620.92. Price gainers equaled decliners at 21 each, but Development Finance, the most capitalised share, fell one rupee to 269.

"Although profit-taking seems to be over, and results coming out are good, investors want to see whether the index will fall if they keep out," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.

Profits for the nine months to 31 December, 1996 of Tea Smallholder had risen 36 percent to 49.50 million rupees. Kegalle Plantations showed a rise of 43 percent to 64.72 million for the same period. James Finlay profits for the 12 months to December 31, 1996 had nearly doubled to 68.14 million rupees.

Turnover was 27.1 million rupees on 536,739 shares, supported by local institutional buying of 70,000 Development Finance Corporation shares. Foreign buying was 805,364 rupees, and selling 19.6 million.
"Trading will be thin until foreign activity returns after Chinese New Year," said Rohan Fernando, a trader at CT Smith.
